Altered Images · One-letter study · Graphics pass

Elastic type meets liquid surface

A visual brief for the standalone one-letter deformation study. Aim for the soft, varied stretch of Diverse Stretched with the glossy, reflective liquid material of Liquid Watch—translated into a legible, responsive real-time browser effect.

Visual references

Use each reference for the quality named below. These source images are externally hosted and need an internet connection to display. The local examples further down are embedded directly in this file.

Current study and material/timing cues

What to make

  • Use the existing drawn path to guide where deformation begins and travels.
  • Create local, varied stretches and blisters along the path; avoid one uniform balloon or a sharp spike.
  • Keep the letter recognisable, including its counters and gaps, as far as possible.
  • Make it feel soft, elastic and wobbly, with a dense glossy surface, strong reflections and visible depth.
  • Use bold saturated synthetic colour with clear contrast. Avoid grey, pastel and muddy tones.
  • If rupture and deflation already exist, improve their timing and leave a soft, rich residue attached to the letter. Keep loose droplets restrained.

Scope and implementation

Work only in the standalone one-letter study. Preserve its existing drawing interaction, controls and project structure unless a small change is essential to the visual result. Inspect the geometry, deformation, material, lighting and animation before editing. Prefer extending the current implementation and using art-directed real-time techniques over adding a large dependency or attempting full fluid simulation. Keep performance suitable for a live browser performance.

Codex: implement and verify

  1. Briefly identify the files controlling geometry, deformation, materials, lighting and animation.
  2. Make the focused graphics changes in the existing study.
  3. Run it in the browser; inspect the silhouette, path-driven stretching, material and collapse/aftermath.
  4. Fix obvious visual or runtime problems.
  5. Report files changed, how to run it, what was checked and remaining limits.

Do the implementation and browser check; do not stop after describing a plan.

Reference sources: Erich Gordon, Diverse Stretched; Tektura Studio, Liquid Watch; Mossawi Studios, Type Fluid Experiment. Source images remain the creators’ work; this brief uses them as visual references.
